description: Unified synthetic knowledge base for Bengaluru's emergency response ecosystem. Contains hospitals, ambulances, road network, traffic signals, emergency SOPs, specialists, ICU facilities, cardiac care centres, and trauma centres. Designed for AI-driven emergency dispatch, ambulance routing, and hospital selection.

routing_hints.stemi_routing: Filter cardiac_care where primary_pci_capable=true AND 24x7_service=true, sort ascending by door_to_balloon_time_minutes. Best: Sri Jayadeva (38 min) > Narayana (42) > Manipal OAR (48) > Apollo BG Rd (50) > Fortis (52).
routing_hints.polytrauma_routing: Filter trauma_centers where trauma_level=I AND neurosurgery_available=true AND ct_scan_24x7=true. Best: Victoria (MCI 80), Manipal OAR (helipad), Apollo BG Road (helipad).
routing_hints.ecmo_routing: Filter icu_facilities where ecmo_capable=true. Only 4 units qualify: ICU-001 Manipal MICU, ICU-002 Manipal CICU, ICU-003 Narayana CICU, ICU-006 Apollo MICU.
routing_hints.mci_routing: Filter trauma_centers, sort descending by mass_casualty_capacity. Top 3: Victoria (80), Manipal OAR (60), Apollo BG Road (55).
routing_hints.air_transfer: Filter trauma_centers where helipad=true: Manipal OAR, Apollo BG Road, Narayana Health City.
routing_hints.burn_routing: Filter hospitals where specialties contains Burns & Reconstructive Surgery. Primary: Victoria Hospital (Burns Unit). Secondary ICU: BGS Gleneagles (Burn ICU, ICU-016).
routing_hints.paediatric_routing: Filter icu_facilities where icu_type in [Pediatric ICU, Neonatal ICU]. Best: IGICH PICU, Narayana NICU, St Johns NICU, Cloudnine NICU.

value.title: Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest â€“ Adult
value.activation_trigger: Caller reports unresponsive patient with absent or agonal breathing; confirmed by dispatcher via phone-CPR protocol
steps: Dispatcher confirms scene safety and initiates phone-guided CPR immediately
Dispatch nearest ALS ambulance within 60 seconds of call receipt
Transmit alert to closest cath-lab-capable hospital via ERSS 112 portal
Paramedic on scene: confirm cardiac arrest, start high-quality CPR at 100â€“120 compressions/minute
Apply AED / manual defibrillator; analyse rhythm within 2 minutes of arrival
Establish IV/IO access; administer Adrenaline 1 mg IV/IO every 3â€“5 minutes
Secure airway with supraglottic device or endotracheal intubation; avoid interruption to compressions >10 s
Identify and treat reversible causes (4Hs and 4Ts protocol)
Transmit 12-lead ECG to receiving cardiologist while en route
Perform continuous CPR during transport; notify hospital ETA and ROSC status
On ROSC: maintain SpOâ‚‚ 94â€“98%, SBP >90 mmHg; initiate targeted temperature management if indicated
Direct transfer to Cath Lab bypassing Emergency if STEMI-equivalent post-ROSC ECG
value.dispatch_protocol: Single ALS unit + supervisor notification; STEMI alert activated if ECG confirms; nearest cardiac centre pre-alerted via hotline
escalation_triggers: No ROSC after 20 minutes of resuscitation
Refractory VF/pVT after 3 shocks
Suspected PE or tension pneumothorax as cause
Paediatric cardiac arrest (activate SOP-007)
Mass-casualty event with multiple arrests

value.title: ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) â€“ Pre-hospital
value.activation_trigger: 12-lead ECG transmitted from field showing â‰¥1 mm ST elevation in â‰¥2 contiguous leads, or LBBB with clinical ischaemia
steps: Dispatcher triages chest-pain call; dispatch ALS ambulance with 12-lead ECG capability
Paramedic acquires and transmits 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of patient contact
Administer Aspirin 325 mg PO + Ticagrelor 180 mg PO if no contraindication
Establish IV access; administer Heparin 60 IU/kg IV bolus (max 4000 IU) per physician order
Supplemental Oâ‚‚ only if SpOâ‚‚ <94%; continuous cardiac monitoring and pulse oximetry
Transmit ECG to on-call Interventional Cardiologist at designated cardiac centre
Activate STEMI hotline; receiving hospital prepares Cath Lab for direct admission
Transport with lights and sirens; target door-to-balloon time <90 minutes from first medical contact
Bypass Emergency Department; transfer directly to Cath Lab on arrival
Paramedic handover to cath-lab team with medication log and ECG strip
value.dispatch_protocol: ALS unit dispatched; STEMI network alert sent simultaneously to top 3 nearest cath-lab hospitals; hospital with earliest slot confirmed within 5 minutes
escalation_triggers: Cardiogenic shock (SBP <90 mmHg despite fluids)
Ventricular arrhythmia en route
Patient deteriorates to cardiac arrest (activate SOP-001)
Cath Lab unavailable at primary centre â€“ reroute to secondary
Symptom onset >12 hours â€“ consult cardiologist for fibrinolysis decision

value.title: Major Trauma â€“ Polytrauma / High-Energy Mechanism
value.activation_trigger: MOI includes RTA at >60 km/h, fall >6 m, pedestrian struck, penetrating torso injury, or GCS â‰¤13 at scene
steps: Scene safety confirmed; bystander first-aid instructed via ERSS dispatcher
Dispatch ALS ambulance + trauma supervisor; notify nearest Level-I Trauma Centre
C-ABCDE assessment: control catastrophic haemorrhage with direct pressure / tourniquet
Cervical spine immobilisation with collar and long backboard
Airway management: jaw thrust / NPA; RSI if GCS â‰¤8 or airway compromise
Two large-bore IV lines or IO access; administer Tranexamic Acid 1 g IV over 10 min if <3 h from injury
Permissive hypotension: target SBP 80â€“90 mmHg in penetrating trauma, 90 mmHg in TBI
Chest decompression if tension pneumothorax suspected (2nd ICS MCL or 4th ICS AAL)
Pelvic binder applied for suspected pelvic fracture
Primary survey repeated; FAST exam if trained provider available
Continuous monitoring: ECG, SpOâ‚‚, ETCOâ‚‚, GCS every 5 minutes
Trauma team pre-notification with MIST handover (Mechanism, Injuries, Signs, Treatment)
Rapid transport; limit on-scene time to <10 minutes (scoop-and-run philosophy)
Direct to trauma resuscitation bay; activate massive transfusion protocol if indicated
value.dispatch_protocol: ALS + BLS backup; Trauma Centre pre-alert 10 min before ETA; trauma team assembled at resuscitation bay; blood bank notified for O-negative stock
escalation_triggers: Haemorrhagic shock unresponsive to 2 L crystalloid
GCS drop of â‰¥2 points en route
Suspected open globe or maxillofacial airway compromise
Multiple casualties from same event (activate SOP-009)
Burns >20% TBSA concurrent with trauma (activate SOP-005)

value.title: Acute Ischaemic Stroke â€“ Code Stroke
value.activation_trigger: Positive pre-hospital stroke screen (FAST / BE-FAST) with symptom onset â‰¤4.5 hours or last-known-well time â‰¤24 hours for LVO screening
steps: Dispatcher administers BE-FAST screen; activates Code Stroke if positive
Dispatch ALS ambulance; advise caller: NPO, do not give food or water
Paramedic confirms stroke screen, records exact time of symptom onset or last-known-well
Airway protection; supplemental Oâ‚‚ only if SpOâ‚‚ <94%; avoid hypoglycaemia â€“ check BGL
If BGL <60 mg/dL: D50W 50 mL IV; do NOT treat hypertension unless SBP >220 mmHg
Establish IV access; draw blood samples (CBC, coagulation, renal, glucose)
12-lead ECG to screen for AF
Transmit pre-notification to stroke centre with NIHSS if trained
Do NOT administer anticoagulants or antiplatelets pre-hospital
Direct transfer to CT suite bypassing registration; target door-to-CT <25 minutes
Neurology team standby in CT suite on arrival
If CT confirms no haemorrhage and within window: IV tPA protocol initiated
LVO suspected (NIHSS >6): direct to angio suite for mechanical thrombectomy evaluation
value.dispatch_protocol: ALS unit; Code Stroke hotline activated; neurology team pre-alerted with estimated NIHSS; CT scanner cleared and ready; pharmacy alerted for tPA preparation
escalation_triggers: Rapidly deteriorating GCS or airway compromise â€“ intubate and reassess
Haemorrhagic transformation on CT
Seizure activity en route (activate SOP-012 adjunct)
Symptom onset >4.5 h â€“ reassess for thrombectomy window
Paediatric stroke (â‰¤18 years) â€“ escalate to paediatric neurology

value.title: Major Burns â€“ >20% TBSA or Critical Area Burns
value.activation_trigger: Burns >20% TBSA in adults, >15% in children, or any burn involving airway, face, hands, genitalia, or circumferential limb burns
steps: Ensure scene safety; remove patient from burn source; stop burning process
Clothing removed (not if adherent); jewellery removed from burned areas
Cool burn with running cool water 15â€“20Â°C for 20 minutes; avoid ice
Airway assessment: hoarseness, carbonaceous sputum, singed nasal hair, facial burns â€“ early intubation
RSI with video laryngoscope; anticipate oedematous airway
Estimate TBSA using Rule of Nines; document burn depth (partial vs full thickness)
Establish 2 large-bore IVs through unburned skin if possible; IO if IV inaccessible
Parkland formula fluid resuscitation: 4 mL Ã— weight (kg) Ã— %TBSA â€“ Ringer's Lactate; give half in first 8 hours
Analgesia: Morphine 0.1 mg/kg IV titrated; Fentanyl if haemodynamically unstable
Wound covering: clean non-adherent dressings; do NOT apply creams pre-hospital
Maintain core temperature; prevent hypothermia with blankets
Urine output monitoring via catheter: target 0.5â€“1 mL/kg/h
Transfer to designated Burns Unit; pre-alert with TBSA, depth, mechanism, airway status
value.dispatch_protocol: ALS unit; Burns Centre pre-alerted (Manipal Hospital / St Johns / Victoria Hospital Burns Unit); if airway burn suspected dispatch with anaesthetist-equipped unit
escalation_triggers: Progressive airway oedema or stridor â€“ intubate immediately
Inhalation injury with CO poisoning suspected â€“ 100% Oâ‚‚ via NRB mask
Circumferential chest burns causing restrictive breathing â€“ escharotomy consideration
Chemical burns â€“ activate decontamination protocol
Paediatric burns >15% TBSA â€“ activate SOP-007 adjunct and paediatric burns team

value.title: Obstetric Emergency â€“ Eclampsia / Severe Pre-eclampsia
value.activation_trigger: Pregnant patient >20 weeks with seizures (eclampsia) or BP â‰¥160/110 mmHg with severe features (headache, visual changes, epigastric pain, oliguria)
steps: Dispatch ALS ambulance with obstetric kit; notify nearest hospital with obstetric HDU
Left lateral tilt to relieve aorto-caval compression; airway protection during seizure
Administer Magnesium Sulphate: loading dose 4 g IV over 5â€“10 minutes (20% solution), then maintenance 1 g/hour
Monitor for MgSO4 toxicity: loss of patellar reflex, respiratory rate <12/min; antidote Calcium Gluconate 1 g IV
If seizure persists after 2nd MgSO4 dose: Diazepam 5â€“10 mg IV
Antihypertensive therapy: Labetalol 20 mg IV bolus, repeat 40 mg, then 80 mg every 10 min; or Hydralazine 5 mg IV
Continuous FHR monitoring if device available
IV access Ã— 2; blood samples: CBC, LFT, RFT, coagulation, uric acid (HELLP screen)
Urinary catheter; target urine output >30 mL/hour
Oxygen supplementation to maintain SpOâ‚‚ >95%
Pre-alert maternity unit: parity, gestational age, BP, seizures, medications given
Prepare for emergency caesarean section on arrival
value.dispatch_protocol: ALS with midwife if available; nearest tertiary maternity centre pre-alerted; NICU team on standby; OT cleared for emergency LSCS if gestation >34 weeks
escalation_triggers: Refractory seizures not responding to MgSO4 â€“ consider Phenytoin or general anaesthesia
HELLP syndrome confirmed (thrombocytopenia, elevated LFT, haemolysis)
Abruptio placentae with haemorrhage
Maternal cardiac arrest â€“ modify CPR for pregnancy (activate SOP-001 adjunct)
Fetal bradycardia <100 bpm for >3 minutes

value.title: Obstetric Emergency â€“ Postpartum Haemorrhage (PPH)
value.activation_trigger: Blood loss >500 mL after vaginal delivery or >1000 mL after caesarean section, or any haemorrhage causing haemodynamic instability
steps: Activate PPH protocol; call for immediate obstetric and anaesthetic assistance
Fundal massage; check for retained products, lacerations, uterine atony
Administer Oxytocin 10 IU IM or IV infusion (20â€“40 IU in 500 mL NS at 125 mL/hour)
If atony persists: Misoprostol 800 mcg sublingual or rectal; Carboprost 250 mcg IM every 15 min (max 8 doses)
Establish 2 large-bore IVs; infuse Ringer's Lactate 1â€“2 L rapidly; activate massive transfusion protocol
Send blood for crossmatch; transfuse pRBC in 1:1:1 ratio with FFP and platelets
Apply bimanual uterine compression if uterus soft and bleeding continues
Bakri balloon or uterine packing as temporising measure
Transfer to Operation Theatre for surgical intervention if bleeding not controlled
Tranexamic Acid 1 g IV over 10 min within 3 hours of delivery
Warm all IV fluids; prevent hypothermia with forced-air warming blanket
Continuous monitoring: BP every 5 min, SpOâ‚‚, urine output (target >30 mL/hour)
Neonatology team to manage neonate separately during maternal resuscitation
value.dispatch_protocol: In-hospital protocol primarily; if inter-facility transfer required, dispatch ALS with obstetric team; blood products secured before transport; receiving OT pre-warmed and ready
escalation_triggers: Haemoglobin <6 g/dL with active bleeding
DIC developing (PT/aPTT prolonged, fibrinogen <100 mg/dL)
Haemodynamic collapse unresponsive to resuscitation
Uterine rupture confirmed on examination or imaging
Placenta accreta/increta/percreta requiring hysterectomy

value.title: Paediatric Cardiac Arrest â€“ Infant / Child
value.activation_trigger: Unresponsive child (age <18 years) with absent or abnormal breathing reported to ERSS 112
steps: Dispatcher activates paediatric cardiac arrest protocol; instructs bystander CPR with age-appropriate ratio
Dispatch ALS ambulance with paediatric equipment kit; notify Paediatric Intensivist
On scene: verify cardiac arrest; initiate 15:2 CPR (2-rescuer) or 30:2 (single-rescuer)
Apply paediatric AED pads (or adult pads in antero-posterior position for infants)
Establish IO access if IV failed after 2 attempts; Adrenaline 0.01 mg/kg IV/IO every 3â€“5 min
Airway: BVM with age-appropriate mask ensuring good seal; avoid hyperventilation
Identify paediatric-specific reversible causes: hypoxia, hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, airway obstruction
Check BGL; treat hypoglycaemia with D10W 5 mL/kg IV
Defibrillate if shockable rhythm: 4 J/kg; increase to 4â€“10 J/kg for subsequent shocks
Notify nearest PICU-capable hospital; pre-alert with age, weight, arrest rhythm
Continuous CPR during transport; minimise interruptions to <10 seconds
Post-ROSC: avoid hyperoxia; maintain normoglycaemia; urgent PICU admission
value.dispatch_protocol: ALS with paediatric drug calculator and Broselow tape; Paediatric Emergency notified; if neonate (<28 days) â€“ activate neonatal team at NICU; PICU bed confirmed before departure
escalation_triggers: Refractory arrest >20 minutes despite optimal CPR â€“ consider ECMO if available
Suspected non-accidental injury â€“ safeguarding protocol activated
Congenital heart disease history â€“ specialist cardiac centre referral
Submersion injury with prolonged downtime (activate SOP-011)
Neonate in arrest â€“ activate Neonatal Resuscitation Protocol

value.title: Mass Casualty Incident (MCI) â€“ â‰¥10 Casualties
value.activation_trigger: Single event generating â‰¥10 casualties simultaneously; or declaration by first-responder officer on scene; or NDRF / police activation
steps: First unit on scene declares MCI; transmits METHANE report to ERSS Control Room
Control Room activates MCI plan; notifies all Bengaluru hospitals to activate surge protocol
Incident Commander (Senior Paramedic / EMS Officer) establishes Command Post upwind
Triage Officer initiates START triage at casualty collection point
Colour-coded triage tags applied: Red (immediate), Yellow (delayed), Green (minimal), Black (expectant/deceased)
Separate ambulance lanes: Red casualties to nearest Level-I Trauma Centres; Yellow to secondary hospitals
Prevent ambulance-to-scene saturation: staggered dispatch on Control Room guidance
Establish medical treatment areas: immediate treatment zone, delayed treatment zone, casualty clearing station
Dedicated radio channel for MCI; no personal mobile phone communications by responders
First responder police/fire liaisons establish inner and outer cordon
Blood bank notification: O-negative release; MTP activation at all receiving hospitals
Media officer at outer cordon only; no information to media from scene
NDRF/SDRF liaison for structural collapse, chemical, or mass-casualty specific rescue
After-action review triggered within 24 hours of incident stand-down
value.dispatch_protocol: All available ALS + BLS units; Rapid Response Vehicles; CMC NIMHANS crisis line activated for mental health response; District Health Officer notified; nearest 5 hospitals placed on MCI alert
escalation_triggers: Casualty count exceeds 50 â€“ activate State Disaster Response plan
Hazmat / CBRN suspected â€“ decontamination corridor established
Structural collapse with trapped victims â€“ NDRF activation
Mass casualty paediatric event â€“ all paediatric units mobilised
Terrorist event â€“ BBMP crisis cell and NSG liaison activated

value.title: Acute Poisoning / Toxic Ingestion
value.activation_trigger: Known or suspected ingestion of toxic substance, envenomation, or drug overdose with altered sensorium, haemodynamic instability, or respiratory depression
steps: Identify poison: ask caller for substance name, quantity, time of ingestion; preserve container
Dispatch ALS ambulance; contact Poison Control Centre (1800-425-1213) for antidote guidance
Scene safety: chemical exposure â€“ do not enter without PPE; contact HAZCHEM team
Primary survey: airway protection paramount; GCS assessment
If opioid toxidrome (miosis, bradypnoea, unresponsive): Naloxone 0.4â€“2 mg IV/IM/IN; repeat every 2 min
If organophosphate (cholinergic crisis): Atropine 2â€“4 mg IV every 5â€“10 min until secretions dry; Pralidoxime 1â€“2 g IV
If benzodiazepine overdose: supportive care; Flumazenil only if no seizure history
If tricyclic antidepressant: Sodium Bicarbonate 1â€“2 mEq/kg IV for QRS >100 ms or arrhythmia
Activated Charcoal 1 g/kg PO/NG within 1 hour of ingestion if airway protected and patient alert
Do NOT induce vomiting for corrosive or hydrocarbon ingestion
IV access; fluid resuscitation; ECG monitoring for QT prolongation
Blood samples: paracetamol level, salicylate, BGL, renal, hepatic, ABG, coagulation
Transfer to toxicology-capable Emergency Department; pre-alert with toxin class and symptoms
value.dispatch_protocol: ALS unit; Poison Control Centre on standby; if snake bite â€“ contact nearest antivenom-stocked facility; Victoria Hospital Toxicology Unit pre-alerted for severe cases
escalation_triggers: Refractory seizures despite benzodiazepines
Cardiac arrhythmia secondary to toxin
Methanol / ethylene glycol ingestion â€“ haemodialysis urgently required
Paracetamol overdose >150 mg/kg â€“ N-Acetylcysteine protocol
Paediatric poisoning â€“ activate SOP-008 adjunct

value.title: Drowning / Near-Drowning Rescue
value.activation_trigger: Submersion victim recovered from water; unconscious, absent breathing, or altered GCS reported
steps: Water rescue by trained personnel only; ring-buoy or reach-pole rescue preferred to entry rescue
Horizontal extrication to prevent cardiovascular collapse on vertical removal
Dispatch ALS ambulance; notify nearest hospital with PICU or ICU capacity
Airway management prioritised on land: 5 rescue breaths; begin CPR if pulseless
Remove wet clothing; active external rewarming if hypothermic (<35Â°C)
Do NOT attempt abdominal thrusts to remove water â€“ causes aspiration
Advanced airway with endotracheal tube; 100% Oâ‚‚ initially
Suction airway of water, vomit, debris
IV access; treat hypothermia: warmed IV fluids 40Â°C, warm humidified Oâ‚‚
Treat cardiac arrest using modified algorithm: prolonged resuscitation for hypothermia (core temp target >30Â°C before declaring)
Cervical spine precautions only if diving injury or recreational water sport mechanism
Continuous temperature monitoring; target core >35Â°C
Transfer to ICU-capable hospital; all near-drowning victims require minimum 6-hour observation
value.dispatch_protocol: ALS; if open-water drowning â€“ coordinate with BBMP Lakes Division / Coast Guard equivalent for Karnataka Inland Water Authority; Fire & Emergency Services rescue boats for lake drownings in Bengaluru
escalation_triggers: Core temperature <30Â°C â€“ consider ECMO rewarming at tertiary centre
Persistent VF in hypothermic patient â€“ continue CPR until rewarmed
ARDS developing (SpOâ‚‚ <90% on high-flow Oâ‚‚) â€“ early ICU ventilation
Paediatric drowning â€“ activate SOP-008
Mass drowning event â€“ activate SOP-009

value.title: Fire-Related Emergency â€“ Entrapment / Smoke Inhalation
value.activation_trigger: Active fire with reported victims; smoke inhalation victim; building collapse with entrapment; reported CO poisoning from fire
steps: Scene command by Karnataka Fire & Emergency Services (KFES); EMS in outer cordon until scene cleared
Dispatch ALS ambulance + BLS backup; notify burns and toxicology units
Victim extraction by KFES using SCBA; EMS receives victim at warm zone boundary
Primary survey outside hot zone: airway, breathing, carbon monoxide signs
